input.brief: SipVPN — российский SIP relay для стабильных звонков и CRM-телефонии из-за рубежа

direction.name: The product performs
direction.idea: Software is most convincing when it is doing its job in front of you. Instead of describing features, put small, true, working fragments of the product on the page: the actual control, with real content, responding to the pointer. A colour picker's loupe reads the page's own background and prints its value. A list tool lets you tick an item right there. A type-scale plugin sets the page's own headings. Find the one interaction that is the product and make the hero that interaction; then show each further capability as another fragment at real size. No dashboard collage, no browser frame, no screenshots shrunk until unreadable.
direction.composition: Hero: a short plain headline (4–6vw, left-aligned, upper-left third) and one sentence; the rest of the first screen is the main fragment at actual interface size, sitting directly on the page or on one flat stage colour, large enough to read every label. The fragment is built in HTML and works. Below, capabilities are a single-column sequence, each a row of two parts on a 5/7 split: a two-line statement on one side and the relevant fragment on the other, with the fragments varying in size and shape so the column never becomes a zigzag of equal blocks. Fragments are cropped pieces of interface (a menu, a row, a control, a panel edge), not whole windows. One section pins a fragment while three short statements change it.
direction.typography: The marketing type matches the product's interface type so the fragments and the page feel like one thing. Headline modest; interface text at its true size (13–15px) inside fragments.
direction.colour: Neutral ground. The product's own interface colours provide the colour. At most one flat stage colour behind fragments.
direction.imagery: The interface fragments are the main imagery: build them carefully with real labels, real numbers and sensible states (one hovered, one selected). Around them, two or three real pictures of the customer's world (found with scripts/assets.mjs), never stock of people at laptops.
direction.richness: Fidelity. A fragment with believable content and a real hover state is more interesting than any illustration. Spend the effort there.
direction.pitfalls: A fake interface made of grey bars and circles is the worst outcome; if you cannot build a believable fragment, change direction. Mark each fragment's root element with the attribute data-ui: inside it the product's own conventions apply (1px control borders, small radii, a shadow on its open menu) and the inspector leaves them alone; outside it the house rules hold as usual. data-ui is for cropped fragments only, never for a page wrapper. Do not put the fragment in a browser or laptop frame.

hero.name: Fragment on a shaped stage
hero.blueprint: A neutral ground. The headline occupies the upper-left third: two lines at clamp(52px, 5.2vw, 80px), medium weight, flush left on columns 1–6 at a 40px margin, starting 150px down. One supporting sentence at 18px, max 40ch, follows, then the single action as a small rectangular button. The rest of the screen belongs to one flat stage in a saturated colour: it spans columns 5–12, begins 42% down, and bleeds off the right and bottom edges. Its top-left corner is cut with the product's own shape using `clip-path` (a notch, a chamfer or a tab two columns wide), the only decoration on the page. On the stage, 56px in from its left and top edges, sits the main fragment of the interface at true size with labels at 13–15px, built in HTML and working: one panel or control about 620px wide, cropped by the bottom edge, never a whole window and never inside a browser or laptop frame. Mark its root with data-ui. Navigation is a plain row at 28px from the top: wordmark left and four text links right at 15px. Nothing overlaps the headline.
hero.mobile: The headline sits under the wordmark at 10vw on two lines, followed by the sentence at 16px and the button. The stage comes next at full width, bleeding off both sides and the bottom, its corner cut kept at 72px wide. The fragment sits 16px inside it at true size; if it is wider than the screen the right edge crops it rather than scaling it down.
hero.headline: A plain statement of what the product does in three to six words, two lines of up to about 16 characters each at 5.2vw.

motion.name: Shutter image
motion.description: The one hero or showcase image opens from an edge with a clip-path over about 1.1 seconds while the picture inside settles from 1.12 scale to rest. Use it once, on the image that matters most; later images simply are there. Recipe: 'Image shutter' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: Statement with inline thumbnails
sections.blueprint: A centred statement of 18–28 words, four lines at clamp(32px, 4.2vw, 62px), medium or bold weight, leading 1.12, in a block 60–66% of the viewport wide with 22vh of empty ground above and below. Three to five small frames sit inline between words: each is an `inline-block` 0.85em tall and 0.85–1.3em wide, `vertical-align: -0.1em`, radius 0.14em, holding a tightly cropped photograph (or a crop of real interface) of the thing the neighbouring word names. Frames are part of the line, never floating over it, with 0.12em of space either side. No heading above and no paragraph below; the statement is set as a `p`. Directly under the section the page may split into two flat colour halves or begin the first product row, so the thumbnails read as a preview of what follows. On a motif-driven page every frame takes the motif's shape.
sections.mobile: Left-aligned instead of centred, at 8vw with leading 1.15, about seven lines inside 20px margins. Keep at most three inline frames, each exactly one cap-height tall, and make sure none lands at the start of a line. Vertical padding drops to 96px.

sections.name: Call and response column
sections.blueprint: The sequence is shown as what you give and what comes back, in one narrow column 560px wide starting at column 4, or on the page's text axis. Three exchanges, 88px apart. Each opens with a sentence at 20px medium that begins with its order word ('First, install it.' 'Then ask for a chart.'). 16px under it, the call: the literal thing the user enters, in a filled panel one tone off the ground, radius 8px, padding 20px. For a developer tool that is real code in `<pre><code>` at 14px with a working copy button; otherwise it is the product's own input holding real typed text. Under the call, indented 56px, the response: a true-size fragment marked data-ui showing what the product returns. The third response is the finished result and breaks out of the column, 760px wide, running to column 12. The heading, two to four words at 28px, sits 56px above the first sentence.
sections.mobile: The column fills the width with 20px margins. Calls and responses stack without the indent; a 24px gap and a lighter panel tone set the response apart. Code panels scroll sideways inside themselves. The final result runs edge to edge at true size, cropped on the right if wider.

sections.name: Staggered fragment cells
sections.blueprint: A three-column grid of six filled cells with 8px gaps, each cell 420–460px tall and filled one tone off the ground, no outlines. Every cell has two parts: a text part (a title at 17px medium and three lines at 15px in the soft ink, 24px padding) and a real fragment of the interface at true size (a control, a menu, a table slice, a swatch strip) docked flush against the opposite edge of the cell and cropped by it. The stagger is the idea: across the first row cells run text-top, fragment-top, text-top; the second row runs the reverse, so fragments form a checkerboard. Fragments differ in shape and size on purpose. The heading, two to four words at 32–40px, sits left-aligned above the grid with 56px beneath it and no supporting line.
sections.mobile: One column of cells at their natural height with 6px gaps. Every cell runs text first, fragment second, but fragments alternate between docking to the left edge and the right edge, and they are allowed to run off the side of the cell at true size instead of shrinking.

sections.name: One quiet logo row
sections.blueprint: Only for real logos supplied by the project; if none are supplied, set the names in the text face at 22px in the same row and never draw stand-ins. The row reads as a sentence: it opens at the left margin with two to four plain words at 18px (the phrase that introduces the names), vertically centred on the logos, and five to seven logos follow on the same line, spread to the right margin with `justify-content: space-between`. Every logo is normalised to one optical height (28–32px for wordmarks, 36px for compact marks) and one colour, the page ink, using single-colour SVGs with `fill: currentColor`. The band is tall and almost empty: 120–150px of ground above and below the row, no box, no background change and no separate heading. Logos stay still; nothing scrolls or fades at the edges.
sections.mobile: The opening words sit alone on the first line at 17px. Logos follow in a grid of two per row, each 26px tall and left-aligned in its cell, with 36px between rows. Show six at most; there is no sideways scrolling.

sections.name: Plan names, one live figure
sections.blueprint: Plans are a list of names; the price shown belongs to whichever name is selected. Columns 1–6 hold the plan names stacked at about 5vw, leading 1.1, each a `<button>`; the selected one is in the full ink, the others in the softer ink, and the selected name carries a solid dot 0.3em across at its left. Columns 8–12 hold one stage that stays in place while its contents change: the selected plan's price at about 9vw at the top, the period beside it at 18px, a paragraph of three or four lines at 18px saying what that plan includes, and one rectangular button whose label names the plan. Changing plan swaps the stage contents with a 200ms crossfade; the figure's position never moves. Selection follows click and keyboard focus. The middle plan is selected on load. There is no heading: the names are the heading.
sections.mobile: Plan names stack at 10vw, each on its own line. Tapping one opens its stage directly beneath that name (price at 20vw, paragraph at 17px, full-width button) and closes the others, like a large accordion without lines. The middle plan starts open.

sections.name: Accordion of filled tiles
sections.blueprint: A two-part row. Columns 1–4 hold the heading, two to four words at about 4vw, `position: sticky; top: 96px` so it stays while the list scrolls past. Columns 5–12 hold the accordion: each question is a filled tile one step from the page ground, with 8px between tiles, no border and the page's one radius (or its motif's corner). A closed tile is 72px tall with the question at 20px medium on the left, 24px padding, and on the right a plus sign drawn from two 3px bars 16px long. The open tile switches to the accent colour with its assigned ink, the plus becomes a minus by rotating one bar, and the answer appears at 17px, no wider than 52ch. Build each tile as `<details>` with a shared `name` so one opens at a time. Six to nine tiles.
sections.mobile: The heading sits above at 9vw, not sticky. Tiles run full width with 6px gaps, questions at 18px wrapping to two lines, closed height at least 64px. The open tile keeps the accent colour, and answers are set at 16px with 20px padding.

sections.name: A sentence with a blank
sections.blueprint: The closing sentence has a gap in it, and the gap is the form. A sentence of five to eight words is set at about 6vw on two lines, flush left across columns 1–11; there is no separate heading. Where the reader's email (or name, or city) belongs, an `<input>` sits inline on the baseline: a filled block of the one-step tone, exactly one line-height tall and about 7em wide, with the placeholder in the same face and size in the softer ink, no border, and the page's radius or motif corner. The sentence's last word is the submit `<button>`, set in the same type on a block of the accent colour of the same height. Field and button use `em` units so they scale with the sentence. One line at 16px under the sentence, in the softer ink, says what happens after sending. Nothing else is in the section.
sections.mobile: The sentence is set at 10vw on two lines; the input drops to a line of its own between them at full width and one line-height tall, and the final word, as the button, ends the second line. The explaining line follows at 15px.

sections.name: A footer of tiles
sections.blueprint: The footer is the last two rows of a board: filled tiles with 8px gaps and 8–12px outer margins, every cell used. Upper row, each tile 220px tall: a statement tile in columns 1–4 with one sentence at 24px top-left and the legal text at 12px bottom-left; a navigation tile in columns 5–7 with a plain list at 16px; a tile in columns 8–9 giving the city and local time as text; an email tile in columns 10–12 with the address at 20px as a link, bottom-left. Lower row, 320px tall: a tile in the ink colour spanning columns 1–8 with the wordmark set large (about 9vw) and centred, and a tile in the accent colour in columns 9–12 with a two-to-four-word invitation top-left at 28px and an arrow, drawn as inline SVG with 4px strokes, in its bottom-right corner; the whole accent tile is a link.
sections.mobile: Two columns of tiles with 6px gaps: the wordmark tile full width first at 160px tall, the accent tile full width next, then navigation and email side by side, then time and statement. Every tile keeps 20px padding and top-left text.

references.name: Rows
references.idea: Radical understatement: a product about simple lists is sold with a 27px headline, 12px copy and a column of small live demos, each proving one interaction.
references.hero: Warm off-white page, almost empty. Everything hangs on one vertical line 27% in from the left. A small striped-letter logo mark sits there near the top; 220px lower comes a two-line headline at only 27px (under 2vw), then three lines of 13px body about 370px wide, then a near-black rectangular button with 4px corners beside a text link with an arrow. A single grey sign-in link sits in the top-right corner; there is no navigation bar. More than 80% of the viewport is blank. At the bottom edge the first feature module peeks in: grey demo panel left, short text column right.
references.type: Suisse Intl only, weight 450–500, tracking −0.04em. Headline 27px, feature headings about 16px on two lines, body 12px. Three sizes in total, no uppercase and no display moment; hierarchy comes from weight and empty space alone.
references.colour: #f5f6f1 #e6e7e1 #1a191d #ffffff #c7372f #3aa56a — Warm paper off-white with slightly darker grey-green demo panels and near-black type; colour appears only inside the UI as priority dots, outlined status pills and one green or red action button.
references.imagery: No pictures: small live-rendered fragments of the app (two or three white list rows with dots, status pills, avatars and a visible cursor) sit in flat grey panels of fixed 368px width with barely rounded corners.
references.layout: One content block about 650px wide, offset left of centre, repeated down the page: 368px demo panel plus a 245px text column, top-aligned, separated by 200px or more of empty space. The logo mark sticks to the top-left corner on scroll. Footer is one line.

sections.description: The repeating module: a flat grey panel roughly 368px wide and 120–190px tall holding a tiny mock list (white rows with 6px radius, a coloured numbered dot at left, task title, an outlined status pill, an avatar, a chevron) and often a cursor mid-action. To its right, 20px away and top-aligned, a medium-weight heading of one or two lines and two short paragraphs at 11–12px in a column only 245px wide. Modules never alternate sides; they stack with large gaps.

The closing block keeps the same narrow measure: a three-line paragraph at 13px, then the identical button and arrow-link pair from the hero, left-aligned on the text column's axis. After a long gap a single hairline spans the 650px block and under it sits one row of tiny footer text: brand line at left, six links and a copyright strung along the right.

steal: Set the headline at near-body size (under 2vw) and let empty space, not scale, give it importance.
Explain each feature with a tiny cropped fragment of real UI in a fixed-width flat panel, one interaction per panel, with the cursor left visible.
Hang the whole page on one off-centre left edge and never break it, logo and footer included.

references.name: Dabbit
references.idea: The colour picker demonstrates itself on the page: its loupe sits in the hero reading the site's own background hex, and every feature is shown as a real fragment of the app.
references.hero: Near-black viewport split exactly in half by a one-pixel vertical hairline. Left half: a small chrome four-petal logo top-left at a 40px margin, then two thirds of empty dark, then everything else anchored bottom-left: a one-line 30px medium-weight headline, three lines of grey 18px copy, a light pill button beside an outlined pill, and a tiny note. Right half: a 450px rounded square with a thin iridescent border, the app's loupe, empty except for a centre crosshair dot and a small chip reading the hex of the page's own background. Eight pastel dots and lozenges drift across the top-right like spilled swatches.
references.type: InterVariable only. Headline a modest 30px medium with -0.025em tracking; section heads about 22px; cell titles 15px; body 16px grey. Largest text is 3.3vw. Hierarchy comes from white against grey rather than size; hex values use tabular figures.
references.colour: #141416 #2b2b2e #f4f3f2 #9a9aa0 #f4a48c #d4c6e6 — Charcoal ground, off-white and grey text, no brand accent. All colour comes from the product: pastel swatches, tonal scales, and a thin prismatic edge on the loupe and logo. Neutral-cool.
references.imagery: Live-drawn UI fragments on canvas: swatch strips, eleven-step scales, contrast tables, a Figma plugin panel, each in a slightly lighter rounded panel. A chrome 3D logo and chrome price numerals are the only non-UI images.
references.layout: 40px outer margins; the hero's centre hairline becomes a three-column then four-column hairline grid. No section changes background; rhythm is small eyebrow, heading, grid, repeat. Text sits top-left in every cell.

sections.description: A three-column grid ruled by one-pixel hairlines with no card backgrounds. Each cell is over 400px tall: 15px white title and three lines of grey copy, plus a real UI fragment docked above or below (a swatch history strip, a tonal scale, a contrast table, a ten-by-ten colour matrix). Rows alternate text-over-mock and mock-over-text so the grid staggers. The loupe square from the hero reappears floating across cell boundaries.

A four-column, three-row grid of minor features divided by hairlines. Each item is a 14px title prefixed by a tiny coloured glyph (dot, square, triangle or dash, one shape per column, in the app's pastel colours) and two lines of grey text. No icons, no cards, no hover chrome.

Left third: small grey eyebrow, a 22px heading, one paragraph. Right: the price rendered as huge chrome 3D numerals about 150px tall with the loupe square overlapping them, a tiny qualifier beside, and a plain four-line checklist beneath. No pricing card, no border, no tiers.

Closing block centred on the same dark ground: the chrome four-petal logo enlarged to about 200px, pastel shapes scattered widely around it, a two-line 22px sentence, the same two pill buttons, then a one-line footer with copyright left and seven text links right.

steal: Make the hero demo sample the page itself: the tool reports the site's own background value, proving the product without a screenshot.
Build feature grids from hairlines and real UI fragments instead of bordered cards and icons, alternating text-above and mock-above per row.
Keep the headline small (30px) and anchored bottom-left so the product object, not the slogan, owns the first viewport.

references.name: Butter
references.idea: A video editor presented as a bunch of collectable objects: 3D keychain charms in the hero and squircle effect tiles that behave like app icons everywhere else.
references.hero: Soft grey vertical gradient, darker at the top, fading to near-white. Two floating light-grey rounded capsules form the nav: the left holds the script logo, five links and a kebab; the right holds Login and a black button. A 3D bunch of keychain charms (orange carabiner, black letter keycap, chrome ring, magenta disc, steel key, green script tag) hangs from the top edge at centre, overlapping the nav and stopping just above the headline. The headline is one centred line at 7.5vw in regular-weight grotesk spanning 75% of the width, with a 24px sub-line and a black rounded-rectangle button beneath. The bottom 35% is empty.
references.type: DieGrotesk regular at 107px for the one-line headline, near-zero tracking, mixed case; the same face at 24px and 16px below, so a 4.5x then 1.5x step. ABC Diatype for tiny labels inside product panels. The logo is brush-script lettering used as an image.
references.colour: #e8e8e8 #f5f5f5 #1e1e1e #0a0909 #ff3fd8 #19e319 — Grey-to-white ground with black type and black product panels. Saturated colour (magenta, green, orange, holographic pastels) appears only on 3D objects, effect tiles and the footer wordmark.
references.imagery: Live 3D charms with chrome and plastic materials; black editor UI panels with 24px radius; many small squircle video tiles showing halftone, glitch and type-poster effects; a full-width extruded script wordmark.
references.layout: 96px side margins for the nav capsules, a centred content column and very large vertical gaps between blocks. Light grey throughout, with black product panels sliding in from below; ends on a full-bleed wordmark.

sections.description: A single row of seven client logos in black spans the full width, then a long gap, then a centred three-line statement at about 32px, roughly 580px wide, with five small squircle thumbnails (app-icon sized, each a different texture or brand tile) set inline between words like emoji. Words resolve from blurred pale grey to sharp black with scroll, so the last line is still soft and tinted.

A black rounded panel about 690px wide slides up from below: a timeline with timecode, ruler ticks and a track of squircle clips, each clip a vivid texture (halftone horse, glitch stripes, red type poster). One clip is lifted out of the track, enlarged and rotated a few degrees, overlapping the panel's top edge. A second black panel shows a labelled library grid of the same tiles.

Text link columns sit at the top; below them the script wordmark is blown up to the full width and cropped by the bottom edge, drawn in solid black with a thick extruded underside in a holographic pink, blue and cyan gradient and a registered mark at its top right.

steal: Hang a cluster of 3D branded charms from the top edge so it overlaps the nav and points down at a one-line headline.
Set small squircle thumbnails inline between the words of a statement and resolve the words from blurred to sharp on scroll.
End on the script wordmark at full width with a holographic extruded underside, cropped by the bottom edge.
references.media: A 3D keyring about 380x340 hangs from the top edge over the centred headline, about 15% of the fold. After that video is the main medium, 45 muted looping product recordings and client clips in 32px-radius frames: 641px splits alternating sides, a dark app window that pans in from the right in a pinned section, stacked videos swapped by a tab list, and a rail of 9:16 clips bleeding off both edges; no video in the hero.
references.motion: About 2-2.5s of empty grey before the nav, keyring and headline arrive, the headline split into characters that fade and rise. Lenis; one 1800px pinned section slides the statement off left while the app window grows to nearly full width; word spans rise over 0.8s cubic-bezier(0,0,0,1) on 100 elements, four cards stagger in at 0.2-0.5s delays, and the ground steps from #fafafa to #ededed over 1s.
